$comment: Source of truth for feature flag METADATA. Debt is always DERIVED from this file by cli/src/flag-debt.js — never stored here. See docs/flag-debt.md.

conventions.$comment: frameworkPaths belong to NO flag: they are shared infrastructure serving every flag, so they never count as owned code nor as touch points. Matched as path fragments, which is why the backend entry has no src/ prefix — it also covers src-test/.

flags.description: Gates the paid upgrade flow that turns a trial account into a second, productive tenant: the frontend entry point plus the backend paywall that authorises it.
flags.ttlNote: PLACEHOLDER — created + 90 days. Nobody has committed to this sunset date yet; the flag owner must replace it with the real removal target.
flags.$symbolsComment: Grep terms that find every reference to this flag. The last two are needed because a touch point may reach the flag's code without naming the flag: runtime-routes.jsx only lazy-imports UpgradePage.
flags.$pathsComment: Owned paths only — code that exists because this flag exists and is deleted with it. src/com/etendoerp/go/rest/EtendoGoJwtServlet.java is a touch point, not owned.
flags.$knownGapComment: USER-ACCEPTED VISIBLE DEBT (scorecard demo). src/com/etendoerp/go/payment/TenantPlanService.java (markProductive, resolvePlan) has no unit test and is not exercised by TenantPaywallServiceTest. The unit-level spec below is declared expected:true and is intentionally deferred, so this flag carries the tests penalty on purpose rather than reading as a clean sheet. Asserting the AD_Preference persistence itself stays integration scope and is NOT what the deferred unit spec would cover.

deferredItems.note: The two ends bucket users on different identities: the frontend sends localStorage.sf_auth_user (the ERP admin username) as OpenFeature's targetingKey, while the backend targets the account email. Harmless today because the local InMemoryProvider ignores the targeting key entirely, and a CORRECTNESS BLOCKER the moment a targeting-aware control plane lands — wiring Mixpanel first would bake per-user bucketing divergence into live rollouts, where it is invisible in aggregate. Must be closed BEFORE the swap, not after.
refs: docs/feature-flags.md — 'Open: targeting keys do not match'

com.etendoerp.go docs/feature-flags-and-tenant-upgrade.md — section 'Targeting key — OPEN, must be settled before a targeting-aware provider lands', and Mixpanel migration checklist step 4 (commit bd068495)

deferredItems.note: The environment picker does not show which plan a tenant is on. The backend already ships the data — GET /sws/go/environments returns a per-environment 'plan' field (EtendoGoJwtDalHelper.java:346, via TenantPlanService.resolvePlan). Rendering it needs a change in the @etendosoftware/etendo-go-core package plus a version bump here, which is why it is deferred rather than done inline.

flags.$deferredItemsComment: Open items this flag carries that are NOT test gaps: unscored in v0, but rendered on the flag's card so the TTL surfaces them before the control-plane swap starts rather than during it.

unit.note: user-accepted debt — unit test deliberately deferred, nobody is writing it

flags.$testSpecsComment: expected:true means the spec is agreed but not written yet (pending Tester). Those paths are a contract: they are where the specs are expected to land, following each suite's existing naming convention.
